resources.string: Hi. Unhook breaks the auto-open habit.
Three promises before we touch a single permission:
Everything runs on this phone. There is no account, no server, and this app has no INTERNET permission — it physically cannot phone home. One tap in Settings wipes everything, forever.
Unhook exists to give you time back, including from itself. It will use about 15 seconds of your day. No feeds, no streaks, no guilt.
Every permission is explained in plain English before Android asks, and you can revoke any of them whenever you want.
Pick the apps you open on autopilot. Unhook will interrupt the habit loop — gently, one change at a time.
Skip for now — I just want the baseline numbers first
Unhook needs to notice when a trigger app opens. Android only allows this through the “Usage access” special permission.
What we can see: WHICH app opened, WHEN, and for how long. That is all.
What we can never see: screen content, keystrokes, notifications, photos, messages, contacts. Unhook has no code that could read them, and no internet to send them anywhere.
You can revoke this any time in Settings. Unhook will keep showing your dashboard and stop watching.
Why we need “Display over other apps”
When a trigger app opens, Unhook draws a brief pause screen (about 6 seconds) over it — a breath, one question, then you decide.
What this allows: showing that pause screen the moment you open Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and friends.
What it does not do: record the screen, block touches after the pause, or change what other apps do.
Skip — pauses will be less reliable, but nothing breaks

One quiet notification shows that monitoring is on. And at most once a week you get your Insight Report. That is every notification you will ever see from Unhook — it is hard-coded, not a promise we might break.
Before we start, Unhook verifies its own integrity and creates the encryption keys for your local database. Your data will be encrypted with a key that never leaves this phone’s secure hardware.
Integrity verified • encryption ready (AES-256, hardware-backed key)
WARNING: this install is not signed like the one that created your data. Reinstall from a trusted source.
Not yet — tap the button below
One breath first, then you decide.
You open %1$s about %2$d times today, usually around %3$s. Still want in?
You have opened %1$s %2$d times today. Still want in?
You asked for this limit. No guilt if you need to break it — but if it can wait, tomorrow-you will be glad.
This is your scheduled quiet window. If something genuinely needs you in there, that is allowed — it just gets logged so the numbers stay honest.
Stand up, walk to the farthest room or around the block. The urge usually fades before you get back.
Oldest trick in the book because it works: hands busy, brain reset.
Neck rolls, shoulder shrugs, touch your toes. Wind-down for the body, wind-down for the scroll urge.
Open the thing you were avoiding and give it one pomodoro. The phone can wait 25 minutes.
Write the one thing on your mind right now. Naming it beats numbing it.
Not a story, not a post — an actual person. Two lines. Real contact beats the feed.
Integrity warning: app data or signature does not match this install. Consider Erase Everything and a clean reinstall.
Grant Usage access to see app numbers
This week: %1$d trigger opens • %2$s reclaimed • %3$s%% vs last week
Rough stretch — goals softened for 24 h. Smaller steps count.
Was your last long session actually worth it?
This wipes the usage database, the ML model, encryption keys and all settings. There is no server copy — this is the only copy. The app then returns to onboarding.
After this, the deleted database cannot be decrypted even by this app: the key that unlocked it will be destroyed. This cannot be undone.
Quiet, permanent notice that Unhook is watching app switches on-device
On-device only. Tap to open your numbers.
At most one per week: your triggers, trends, and one suggestion
Down %1$d%% vs last week — that is real progress.
Up %1$d%% vs last week — no guilt, let’s aim smaller.
About the same as last week — steady is fine.
